title: Anti-Slosh Tank Engineering is the #1 Failure Mode for Liquid-Carrying Drones
context: Splash carries ~15ml water reservoir. During flight maneuvers, liquid slosh creates a pendulum effect that destabilizes the PID loop, causing immediate crashes.
what_was_found: Multiple Reddit threads (r/drones, r/diydrones) and Google AI Mode research confirm: unbaffled water tanks are the single most common cause of liquid-carrying drone crashes. The fluid momentum during stops/turns shifts CG unpredictably, sending the FC into chaotic over-correction.
fixes_identified: Internal baffles — 3D print walls with tiny holes inside the tank (verified by multiple builds)
Open-cell anti-slosh foam — race car fuel cell material, restricts free fluid movement
Center-mount + vertical partition — slim tank design under frame center keeps CG stable as fluid drains
TPU material for tank — flexible, absorbs some slosh energy
source: Hour 7 Competitor Analysis — Reddit r/drones, r/diydrones, Google AI Mode
action: CAD design for anti-slosh tank REQUIRED before first flight. Test with water-filled tank on bench (no props) — verify CG doesn't shift during rapid attitude changes.
